calls.bear_case: Spending now exceeds cash flow (~$34B spent last quarter); the raise anticipates needs that may not materialise if AI demand cools.

calls.video_title: Meta Stock Analysis: Buy or Sell? (My Final Verdict)
calls.price_at_call: DCF fair value $913 (stated); forward P/E 21 (stated); 40%+ upside over 12-18 months (stated); current price drops out of the auto-captions
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated (was BUY 2026-10-26; no flip) — he reiterates Meta as a top-10 / one of the best stocks you can buy right now and holds it as one of his larger positions, after updating his DCF for the post-earnings fall (stock +4% after-hours, then -8% the next day).
calls.base_case: Revenue $64.2bn, up 26% YoY; ad impressions +10% with higher price per ad and engagement, delivered with 12% fewer employees; Q4 revenue guided to about $74.5bn at the midpoint.
calls.bull_case: AI-driven ad targeting and productivity are lifting the core business; Muse personal agent is already succeeding (not yet monetised) and management expects >10x serving-efficiency improvement next year from off-peak use, more efficient models and inference optimisation.
calls.bear_case: Free cash flow turned negative (-$2.1bn in the quarter); he now models -$10bn this year, -$41bn next year and -$3bn the year after, positive only from 2029 ($60bn+). Cash $82.4bn vs $83.7bn debt, capex over $135bn this year and an estimated $150-175bn next year; dilution concerns from a new share class and a possible Zuckerberg stock sale for a California billionaire tax.

calls.video_title: My Favorite Stocks Are a Screaming Buy Today
calls.price_at_call: under $700 (stated; back under $700, down ~5% intraday after being up 5-7% on the print)
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated (most recent prior explicit was BUY; no flip) — title frames his favorites as a screaming buy. Meta still undervalued after an amazing quarter: revenue +26% to $64B, ad impressions +10%, price per ad +14%, daily active people +3%, and Muse personal-agent traction (10M set up in ~6 weeks). Says if the stock goes lower he will pick up more shares; the -5% flip from green to red is an opportunity, not a broken business.
calls.bull_case: Muse monetises sooner than Meta's usual playbook (transaction fees, subscriptions, ads, enterprise), existing Muse users already generate several hundred dollars a year each in family-apps revenue, and Reality Labs losses shrink — $3.5B lower in 2027, trending to profitability.
calls.bear_case: Capex has doubled year-on-year and pushed free cash flow negative — the first quarter since 2012 with no FCF — plus a $9.89B state-attorneys-general settlement charge that could grow, and a planned Class C non-voting raise that would be painful if done under $700 rather than nearer $800.

calls.thesis: HOLD reiterated (was HOLD 2026-10-12; no flip) — 'well worth holding through the capex cycle'; monetisation power, not pricing power: ad prices +12% YoY while impressions rose +14% and ad revenue +27%, because advertisers bid more for better-converting, more targeted ads across a still-growing daily-active base in every region. Expects a super-strong quarter on Wednesday.
calls.base_case: The business prints a very strong quarter and he holds through the spending cycle.
calls.bull_case: Monetisation keeps compounding — more ads, higher prices per ad, better returns for advertisers — funded by the core apps, including the Muse push.
calls.bear_case: Management likely raises capex guidance again, which could spook investors even on a strong print; the quarter's debate will be Zuckerberg's spending, not the results.

Says buy before Oct 21 earnings if you own none — 75% before / 25% after, or 50/50 risk-neutral; he personally holds a large position and would only add after earnings.

calls.bear_case: CapEx guide $130-145B may rise on component costs; spending beyond operating cash flow (~$130B annualised) would concern him.
